interface.title: Potato annotation tool – 'Simple Single-Choice Example' (simple-radio-selection config)
interface.field: NLP / data annotation (any field that needs human labels on text, audio, images or video)
interface.stage_of_work: data labeling / building a corpus with human judgments before analysis or model training
interface.what_it_is_for: Registered annotators work through a queue of text items and give each one a single-choice label from a scheme set in YAML. Each person's answers are saved separately, so labels can later be exported and compared across annotators.

Nothing was uploaded; the annotation page has no upload control.

features.name: Single-choice label panel with number-key shortcuts
features.general: Show one item with a fixed list of mutually exclusive categories. Pick one with the mouse or a number key, re-pick to correct it, and save the choice as you move on.
features.specific: The 'What food does this text make you want to eat?' radio group (Pizza 1 … Tacos 5) under the 'Text to Annotate' box. Each option shows a key-hint chip, and keys 1–5 select it.
steps: read the item text in the 'Text to Annotate' box
click a radio button or its label, or press its number key (1–5)
press a different number to change the choice before or after leaving
move on with Next/ArrowRight. The choice is saved. The badge stays 'Not labeled' right after a choice and turns 'Labeled' only after you navigate away and back.
serves_tasks: Pick one category for the current item
Correct an earlier answer and have the correction kept
Label the same items as a second person, agreeing on some and disagreeing on others

features.name: Queue navigator with progress, labeled-status badge, skip-to-unlabeled and jump-to-number
features.general: Move through a long list of items one at a time. A counter shows how many you have done, and a badge shows whether this item is done. You can skip, jump to the next or previous unfinished item (wrapping around the ends), or go straight to an item by its number.
features.specific: The top bar: 'Labeled/Not labeled' badge, 'Progress n/1000', 'Instance #k', the Unlabeled ◀/▶ buttons, the '#' box with Go, and the Previous/Next buttons (also ArrowLeft/ArrowRight).
steps: advance or go back with Next/Previous or the arrow keys; Progress counts only labeled instances
skip an item by pressing Next without answering
press Previous/Next unannotated to land on the nearest unlabeled instance (wraps past #1 to #1000 when nothing earlier is unlabeled)
type an instance number in the # box and press Go or Enter to jump there (the replay found out-of-range numbers are ignored)
read the Labeled/Not labeled badge to confirm the item's state; it updates on navigation, not at the moment of choosing
serves_tasks: Skip an item and come back to it later
Jump to a numbered item and see its saved label

features.name: Per-annotator accounts with resumable sessions
features.general: Each labeler registers and signs in, keeps their own answers and progress, and on returning picks up at the item where they stopped. A second person sees a fresh queue of the same items, so the two sets of labels can be compared.
features.specific: Sign In/Register tabs on the login page (unregistered names are rejected), Logout in the top bar, and separate Progress counters for annotator1 (5/1000) and annotator2 (0→3/1000) over the same instances.
steps: register a username and password on the Register tab
label items; progress and answers are saved under that user
log out and sign back in; work resumes at the last instance with earlier answers intact
register a second user, who starts at Instance #1 with 0 progress and labels the same texts independently
serves_tasks: Create a labeler account and enter the labeling screen
Leave and return, picking up where the work stopped with earlier answers intact
Add a second labeler for agreement
